standard_prerequisites.name: Partial elementary map
standard_prerequisites.statement: A map between subsets is partial elementary when it preserves the truth of formulas on the tuples where it is defined.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the conclusion of the statement.

standard_prerequisites.name: Elementary subsystem
standard_prerequisites.statement: A is elementary in M when the formulas with parameters in A agree.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the hypothesis on both sides.

standard_prerequisites.name: Saturated elementary extension
standard_prerequisites.statement: Every structure has a saturated elementary extension of prescribed large cardinality.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the reduction used in the countable case.

core_obligations: Treat first the countable case: use the previous lemma to replace A and B by the subsystems they generate, extend the isomorphism, and pass to saturated elementary extensions (source lines 1003-1004).

Reduce the general case to the countable one by taking a finite subset of A, closing it under an HF-ordering of M with A as initial segment, and applying the countable case to the finite data (source lines 1006-1007).

proof_roadmap.step: Countable case through generated subsystems and saturated extensions.
General case by reduction to finite data.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled corollary at source lines 1001-1002: for infinite unconfined systems M and N, elementary subsystems A of M and B of N, every isomorphism of the partial structures between A and B is a partial elementary map. The proof (source lines 1003-1007) is a two-stage reduction: the countable case is obtained by replacing each subsystem with the subsystem it generates (which the previous lemma shows to be elementary and isomorphic) and then passing to saturated elementary extensions, and the general case is reduced to the countable one by closing a finite subset of the domain under an HF-ordering with the subsystem as initial segment, so that finite data suffice. The statement records the corollary and neither the reduction nor the use of the finite approximations.
